decisions.reason: As a newly launched software product with its own page and strong fit to the firm's move toward integrated, data-driven airport operations, it is a valuable option to retain while market feedback is still forming.
This connectivity module supports the firm's integration strategy and likely has relatively low carrying cost, so real-options logic favors keeping it on the market until demand becomes clearer.
Although billing software is somewhat less central to the firm's core airside operational offering, it still extends software capabilities and should be kept as a low-cost adjacent option for now.
Equipment monitoring closely matches the firm's installed-base knowledge, maintenance capabilities, and digital service direction, so there is little reason to abandon it early.
Resource management is strategically aligned with airport efficiency and automation goals, and the firm should preserve this option while adoption uncertainty remains unresolved.
A controller safety alert service fits the firm's safety-critical positioning and service expansion, so despite possible certification or sales-cycle uncertainty it is worth keeping open.
